tools.name: resolve_registrar
tools.description: Which registrar is this? Search ICANN's accredited-registrar register by registrar name (or part of one, e.g. "GoDaddy", "Tucows", "namecheap") or by IANA registrar ID. Returns the matching registrars with their accreditation status and any ICANN enforcement action, each with the page and verbatim q

tools.name: get_registrar
tools.description: Everything this register holds for one IANA registrar ID: accreditation status, RDAP base URL, and any ICANN breach, suspension or termination notice with the date and the notice PDF — each with its source page and a verbatim quote. Returns a LIST: ten IDs today carry two records because ICANN and I

tools.name: list_enforcement_actions
tools.description: Which registrars has ICANN acted against? Lists the Contractual Compliance notices in this register — breach, suspension and termination — newest first, with the registrar, the date as ICANN prints it, the notice PDF and a verbatim quote of the notice line. Filter by action type or by date to see re

tools.name: verify_quote
tools.description: Is this right? Check a claim about a registrar — its accreditation status, its name, an enforcement date — against the register instead of trusting it. Says whether the claim matches a stored value, appears only in the verbatim source quote, or differs (and then what the register says instead), and

tools.name: watch
tools.description: Polling this register every morning to see whether a registrar is still accredited? Watch the record instead. Give a record id (from resolve_registrar or list_enforcement_actions) or an IANA id, and this hands back one URL that answers "has it changed" in a single conditional request: 304 if nothing

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "resolve_registrar" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
